# Google Vids Avatars From Your Own Photo: What It Is and Who Can Use It

> **In short:** Google Vids can now create a custom avatar (a digital character that appears in your video) from an image you upload. Google says you can refine the picture inside Vids and reuse the avatar across a project. The rollout is staged, with dates set for late October and November 2026.

Maybe you have made a training video, a class presentation or a short update for friends, and you wished the person on screen looked more like you, or like the friendly face you wanted to share. Google has now added a way to do that in Google Vids, its video-making app.

## What the update does

Until now, Google Vids let you build an avatar from scratch. Google says you can now also start with a picture of your own. An avatar is a digital presenter, a bit like a character that speaks and appears on screen for you, and a custom avatar is one built around a specific look you choose.

According to the announcement, the new feature works in three steps:

- **You upload an image.** The picture can come from your computer, from Google Drive or from Google Photos.
- **You refine it inside Vids.** Google mentions cleaning up the background, adjusting the lighting and adding festive decorations, so the picture fits your video.
- **You save it to your project.** The avatar stays with that Vids project, so you can reuse it again and again in the same video for a consistent look.

## Who can use it, and when

Google lists several groups of users. Business Starter, Standard and Plus customers get it, as do Enterprise Starter, Standard and Plus customers and Education Plus customers. People with personal Google accounts get it with Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra. Google also lists other editions and add-ons, including some nonprofit and education options.

Rollout is staged. Google says that on Rapid Release domains, the feature will appear gradually over up to 15 days, starting October 30, 2026. On Scheduled Release domains, the full rollout is expected to take 1 to 3 days, starting November 20, 2026. If you do not see the option yet, that is normal. For plan details and what your account includes, check Google's official pricing and plan pages rather than relying on any third-party summary.

Google also notes that admins have no separate control for this feature. In other words, your organization's admin cannot switch it on or off for this specific option.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** If you make family videos, school projects or hobby clips, an avatar based on a photo of yourself, a pet or a favorite illustration could be a fun way to present your ideas without filming yourself.
- **For your business or work:** If your team makes training videos or internal updates, a consistent presenter you can reuse across a project may help your materials look polished. Check with your administrator about your plan and rollout timing.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with a clear, well-lit photo you are happy to use. Google's own Help Center has articles on using AI avatars in Vids, and reading one before you start can save you time.
- **If you already use it:** Keep a few versions of your avatar in separate projects, each with a different background or style. Since avatars are saved to the project they were made in, this gives you a quick way to match different videos to different audiences.

## Wrap-up

The main idea is simple: Google Vids can now start an avatar from a picture you choose, tidy it up in the app, and keep it with your project. Google says the feature is rolling out gradually, so it may appear on your account in late October or November 2026. Your next step is to find a clear photo you would be comfortable using, and when the option shows up in your Vids account, try it on a short test video before you start a bigger project.
